text:
Lauren M.: heads up — received customer report of ~150k audit events dropped during yesterday's 3pm spike. they saw gaps in their tenant audit stream :eyes:
Raj P.: link to support thread?
Lauren M.: https://support.example/INC-3421 (redacted) — they saw 503s from ingest and some events backfilled later.
ingest-bot: alert triggered: ingest-503-rate: 0.8% over 10m at 2024-06-14T15:04Z
Tess K.: any KMS errors in logs? if per-event KMS puts/decrypts, that could be a hotspot.
Luis G.: looked at logs — saw KMS Throttling errors around spike window. stack traces -> `com.redwood.kms.Client:429`. Also noticed indexing lag in ES nodes, bulk queue grew.
Samira: are we encrypting per-event with KMS? we designed DEK cache but maybe cache eviction happened under memory pressure.
Raj P.: quick thread: current flow = event -> encrypt(DEK) cached by host (1m TTL) else KMS.Decrypt -> write to kafka -> indexing consumer -> ES. If cache cold, KMS QPS spikes.
Lauren M.: ok immediate ask: increase DEK cache TTL to 5m on ingest hotpath for tomorrow's peak windows?
Tess K.: that helps but compliance asked we rotate keys every 24h; longer cache still ok as long as DEKs stored encrypted in memory only. need security signoff.
security-oncall-bot: flagged for security review — please include threat model for in-memory DEK caching.
Raj P.: alternative short-term: enable batching at producer => reduce KMS ops per event by 10x (encrypt once per batch?). Proposed config:
```
producer.batch.enabled = true
producer.batch.size = 500
producer.encrypt.batch = true
```
Lauren M.: can we do prefix caching too? many events share same tenant and model config — KV cache would avoid decrypt.
Luis G.: indexing side: ES bulk size currently 100 docs. If we relax to 200 and increase bulk_workers to 8, we reduce indexing pressure. cost = more memory + CPU.
Samira: cost tradeoff note: bigger bulk = lower per-doc overhead but higher memory; also less retryable under partial failures.
Tess K.: validation: we added tenant_id to audit schema last quarter — are customers sending old schema? missing tenant_id could cause routing to fallback and double-write? check validator logs.
Raj P.: I found 2.3k events with schema_v=1 in the spike window — validator dropped with 422. We'll need a migration path and better client-side SDK validation.
Lauren M.: short tactical plan:
- ramp DEK cache TTL to 5m on ingest hosts (rollout canary 5%).
- enable producer batching with batch.size=250 (canary).
- increase ES bulk size to 200 on consumer pool.
- add a validator metric: schema_v_reject_count to telemetry.
- open incident if drop_rate >0.5% in next 2 hours.
Samira: +1. Also suggest adding "priority" flag to audit events so we can triage critical events (authz changes) vs telemetry. low-cost route: keep priority as boolean, route low -> cold S3 with async reindex.
security-oncall-bot: noted. Please document privacy impact of priority routing.
Luis G.: action items for infra: update KMS client to cache DEKs with sliding TTL, add circuit-breaker to avoid cascading KMS failures, add fallback path to encrypt with local wrapping key then rewrap later.
Tess K.: vuln triage: if DEK caching has risk vector, mark as low-medium until we have memory scrubbing & attestations.
Lauren M.: can someone draft quick runbook for on-call if ingest backlog >10M events? include steps: pause non-critical indexing, enable fallback S3 sink, notify SEs, escalate to execs with customer impact.
Raj P.: I'll author runbook and push to runbooks/ingest (PR in 5m). cc @Lauren M.
ingest-bot: alert cleared at 2024-06-14T15:38Z :white_check_mark:
Lauren M.: thanks all. We'll review after canary results. :thumbsup:
Samira: leaving note — long-term: consider envelope encryption where we call KMS only at key rotation and use local crypto for per-event ops.
Lauren M.: agree. schedule architecture review next week. end.
